# Ground-Station Coverage Analysis

Phase 7B.1: does adding a second ground station change this project's generality conclusions? The single-station row below is the existing reference scenario (Mumbai, sim.scenario's GROUND_STATION_LAT_DEG/LON_DEG/ALT_M) -- identical to what docs/baseline-results.md reports. The dual-station row adds a second, illustrative real-world polar ground station (Svalbard, 78.23N 15.39E -- sim.scenario.GROUND_STATIONS_DUAL; a real well-known site chosen for a near-polar orbit's genuine per-orbit visibility, NOT a claim about POQUITO's actual ground segment, which this project has no citation for beyond the single Mumbai station). This analysis is purely additive -- it does not change docs/baseline-results.md or any other single-station result.

Contact is elevation-gated: the link is up iff elevation >= the config's minimum elevation (sim/link.py), so this is an elevation-gated capacity model, not an RF link budget. Deadline success ratio = items delivered by their deadline / items generated (sim.metrics). Config C's reference scenario is the dual-station one (docs/baseline-results.md).

## config-a

| Stations | Contact time (s) | Contact time (% of run) | Delivery success rate | Deadline success ratio | TT&C latency p95 (s) | Energy per delivered bit (J/bit) |

| 1 | 1,760 | 1.02% | 91.85% | 2.61% | 39819.86 | 0.000338873 |
| 2 | 10,160 | 5.88% | 99.08% | 18.14% | 18824.58 | 0.000470347 |

Adding the second station increases contact time by 477.3% and changes delivery success rate by +7.23 percentage points for config-a.

## Interpretation

A second, geographically distant ground station can only add contact opportunities (never remove them -- see tests/test_orbit.py's `test_find_passes_with_second_station_has_at_least_as_much_contact`), so the honest question is how much it matters for this mission's actual reported metrics, not whether it helps at all.
